summary: Grant card migration reached [172,146 of 463,836 replaced by 28 July 2026](2026-08-04-sassa-postbank-presentations-western-cape-standing-committee-social-development), and a state payment credential and wallet [entered active development with testing dated November 2026](2026-07-31-sa-operation-vulindlela-q1-2026-progress-report).
developments:
2026-07/08 — of [463,836 active gold cards at 29 April 2026, 172,146 had been replaced by 28 July and 264,263 remained](2026-08-04-sassa-postbank-presentations-western-cape-standing-committee-social-development), roughly 40% of them in two provinces, against a deadline of [31 August 2026](2026-07-24-sa-sassa-gold-cards-deadline-postbank-black-cards). The bank reports 306 replacement sites against a target of 300 plus nine mobile teams, ring-fences customers more than 30km from a site, and plans the rollout from monthly data on where each customer last transacted.

2026-07-31 — the state's own rail moved: the payments modernisation programme [passed from conceptual design into active development of the payment credential, wallet, governance and trust capabilities, with testing against government use cases dated November 2026](2026-07-31-sa-operation-vulindlela-q1-2026-progress-report).

The base holds no statement of how the state credential is meant to relate to the bank-owned rails it would sit beside, which is the question a G2P wallet raises before it raises any other.

summary: The revenue service [published a VAT modernisation consultation paper](2026-08-18-sars-vat-modernisation-consultation) proposing electronic invoicing, an interoperability framework and electronic reporting, [with feedback due 16 October 2026](2026-08-01-south-africa-sars-vat-modernisation-consultation-paper).
developments:
2026-08 — the revenue service [released a VAT modernisation consultation paper](2026-08-18-sars-vat-modernisation-consultation) proposing a digital VAT model combining electronic invoicing, an interoperability framework and electronic reporting, aimed at moving administration off manual processes and retrospective verification and into the systems businesses already run. It follows a 2023 discussion paper and is stated as building blocks rather than a decided design.

The fuller account [describes a five-corner model moving toward VAT auto-assessment, with a phased rollout from 2026/27 and stakeholder feedback due 16 October 2026](2026-08-01-south-africa-sars-vat-modernisation-consultation-paper).

It is a consultation paper, not a rule: no cost to business, exemption threshold, accreditation regime for service providers or legislative vehicle is stated. What has advanced is a published design intention on the largest transaction flow the state touches.

2026-08-31 — the home affairs department [re-advertised its revenue administration system over 275 fixed sites and 230 mobile units, replacing a generic 400-plus listing and making point-of-sale devices and mobile offices the primary transaction channels](2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-home-affairs-revenue-admin-tender), with [only suppliers on the state IT agency's RFB 1183 transversal contract eligible to bid](2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-home-affairs-revenue-admin-tender). It is a tender, not an award: no value, closing date or bidder is held.

summary: A rand-backed stablecoin was [listed on 7 August 2026](2026-08-07-rand-goes-on-chain-as-zaru-hits-luno-global) and [integrated into a merchant payments infrastructure twelve days later](2026-08-19-tan-ezeebit-zaru-digital-asset-merchant-payments), on the issuer's own account of use.
developments:
2026-08-07 — a rand-backed token was [listed on a global exchange for customers in four African countries](2026-08-07-rand-goes-on-chain-as-zaru-hits-luno-global), issued by an authorised financial services provider with a domestic asset manager holding the reserves and a monthly attestation.

2026-08-19 — a merchant payments provider [integrated the token into its infrastructure, letting its commerce partners make and receive payments in it](2026-08-19-tan-ezeebit-zaru-digital-asset-merchant-payments).

Two things the record makes plain and one it does not. The quoted pairs are against dollar tokens, so the on-chain liquidity of the rand token is denominated in someone else's currency; and the account of growing merchant use is the issuer's own, with no transaction count or value published. Whether any of it is business-to-business volume rather than listing activity, the base cannot say.

summary: The instant payment rail reached [905m cumulative transactions by May 2026](2026-05-21-payshap-pivots-to-merchants), a [national QR code standard reached a v1.2 eight-bank cohort](2026-07-13-sarb-qr-plus-checkout), and merger conditions [opened one bank's rail to third parties](2026-08-06-compcom-approves-capitecs-walletdoc-acquisition).
developments:
2026-05 — the instant payment rail [went from 461m cumulative transactions in March 2026 to 905m by May and pivoted toward merchants](2026-05-21-payshap-pivots-to-merchants), having [passed R100bn in value](2026-04-02-payshap-r100bn-national-payment-utility). Payments is the fastest-moving part of this ledger by a wide margin.

2026-07 — a [national payment code standard reached version 1.2 with an eight-bank test cohort](2026-07-13-sarb-qr-plus-checkout).

2026-08-06 — the competition authority [recommended approval of a bank's R400 million acquisition of a payment provider subject to behavioural conditions](2026-08-06-compcom-approves-capitecs-walletdoc-acquisition): the merged entity must make its pay service available to third-party providers technically and commercially capable of integrating with it, may not use confidential information obtained through that access to compete against them, and must treat competing rails no less favourably unless objectively justified. Access to a dominant rail is being set by merger condition rather than by rule, which is a different thing from an access regime and binds only one party.

2026-08-31 — a proprietary QR scheme [claimed more than 600,000 acceptance locations and more than 19 million application inclusions, and was added to a handset maker's wallet](2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-samsung-digital-wallet). The figures are the provider's own. Nothing on this ledger relates it to the bank-led national payment code standard, still at an eight-member test cohort.

summary: One bank reported [digitally active customers up 10% to 3.8m against 9.9m total](2026-08-18-absa-group-1h26-interim-results-booklet), and a city is [removing cash from six service counters](2026-08-20-itweb-cape-town-cashless-council-centres) with no stated route for the unbanked.
developments:
2026-08-18 — a large bank's interim results [put digitally active personal and private banking customers at 3.8m, up 10%, against 9.9m total customers in that segment](2026-08-18-absa-group-1h26-interim-results-booklet), with total technology spend of R8,779m for the half, up 7% and 28% of group expenses. These are one institution's figures, reported group-wide across seventeen countries, so they bound the cost and pace of migration at a single bank and not the sector.

2026-08-21 — a second bank [reported 581 self-service kiosks handling more than half a million transactions a month across over 60 services, dispensing almost 70% of its instant-issued debit cards, 56% of them to entry-level clients](2026-08-21-itweb-nedbank-client-connect-zones).

2026-09-01 — uptake seen from the other side: a city is [extending a cashless pilot to three further service offices, so cash is no longer accepted at six counters](2026-08-20-itweb-cape-town-cashless-council-centres). No figure is published for how many residents at those counters paid in cash before the change, and nothing is stated about an alternative for the unbanked — which is the whole of the inclusion question a cashless counter raises. No regulator series covers any of this.

summary: A domestic bank [went live on China's cross-border payment system in November 2025](2025-11-20-cips-goes-live-standard-bank-sarb-inauguration) and was [jointly authorised as renminbi clearing bank for Africa in June 2026](2026-06-26-standard-bank-icbc-renminbi-clearing-bank-africa).
developments:
2025-11-20 — a domestic bank [went live and was inaugurated at the central bank as the first African direct participant in China's cross-border interbank payment system](2025-11-20-cips-goes-live-standard-bank-sarb-inauguration), with the central bank's governor, the People's Bank governor and the system's chairman present. It was [accredited in April 2025 and licensed in June](2025-11-21-itweb-standard-bank-cips-live-sarb).

2026-06-26 — the same bank and a Chinese counterpart were [jointly authorised as renminbi clearing bank for Africa](2026-06-26-standard-bank-icbc-renminbi-clearing-bank-africa), with operational capacity in the nineteen African countries where the group operates. It is the first clearing bank named after a continent and the first jointly operated by two commercial banks.

Two qualifications the record carries. The nineteen countries are not enumerated in either account. And the designation was made by one foreign central bank, with no African regulator party to it — a continental clearing arrangement constituted entirely outside the continent's own institutions.

summary: Enforcement rose to [140 public warnings and R2.89bn in penalties in 2025/26](2026-07-30-fsca-regulatory-actions-report-2025-26), while the licensing regime for crypto providers [is stated not to reach decentralised finance](2026-08-11-sa-fsca-defi-crypto-regulation).
developments:
2026-07/08 — the conduct regulator's fourth actions report [put 140 public warnings and R2.89bn of penalties on 76 persons for 2025/26, against 107 warnings and R119.8m the year before](2026-07-30-fsca-regulatory-actions-report-2025-26). [Most warnings concerned unregistered providers promoting investment offerings on social media, and about 20% involved impersonation of licensed institutions, the regulator and its own staff among them](2026-08-04-fsca-social-media-financial-scams). [The penalty jump is driven by one deepfake-advertising matter of over R2bn](2026-07-30-fsca-regulatory-actions-report-2025-26), whose reconsiderations were pending at the report date, so the total is not a run rate.

2026-08-11 — the perimeter is stated and it has a hole in it: licensing of centralised crypto-asset service providers is in force, but the regulator [says the model has no purchase on decentralised finance — protocols with no company, board or natural person to hold accountable](2026-08-11-sa-fsca-defi-crypto-regulation) — and plans to attach obligations elsewhere. No instrument for that is published.

2026-04 — separately, [amendment regulations shifted the anti-spam duty in direct marketing to the consumer commission](2026-04-20-cpa-direct-marketing-optout-regs).

progress: Mixed, a biometric successor anchored in Cabinet policy while the register's own exclusions clear on two incompatible counts
summary: Cabinet [approved the white paper anchoring the intelligent population register](2026-04-08-cabinet-approves-revised-white-paper-citizenship), and [2,202,368 blocked identity numbers were unblocked](2026-06-01-dha-blocked-id-numbers-campaign) on a different count from the court-supervised one.
developments:
2026-04-08 — [Cabinet approved the white paper anchoring the conversion of the population register into an intelligent population register, on biometrics, interoperability and real-time integration](2026-04-08-cabinet-approves-revised-white-paper-citizenship), and [the core biometric technology is live for the citizenship portal while the digital identity front end is still being built](2026-02-17-schreiber-2026-state-of-the-nation-debate). The successor had been [announced in June with the green identity book to be de-recognised](2026-06-08-biometric-population-register-unveiled) and [a biometric case-management system and 600 handheld readers tendered](2026-07-07-biometric-case-management-migration).

The exclusions are reported on two counts that do not reconcile. [A national campaign unblocked 2,202,368 identity numbers blocked before November 2022](2026-06-01-dha-blocked-id-numbers-campaign), while [the court-supervised cohort fell only from 384,189 to 377,060 in roughly seven months, with unserviceable addresses given as the obstacle and a deadline running to March 2027](2026-07-17-home-affairs-unblock-identity-numbers-addresses).

Both are the department's own figures and no source states how the two populations relate.

progress: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
summary: [360,000 identity documents sat uncollected](2026-07-31-home-affairs-extends-operational-hours-to-support-final-voter-registration) at the end of July 2026, on the department's own statement; the base holds no prior figure to compare.
developments:
2026-07-31 — the department opened every office nationwide for the final voter registration weekend, [stating that 360,000 identity documents sat uncollected](2026-07-31-home-affairs-extends-operational-hours-to-support-final-voter-registration). A valid document is a precondition of registering to vote, so the count is a measure of exclusion and not of stock control.

It is a first count. No prior figure, no breakdown by office or province and no statement of how long the documents have been waiting is published, so the direction cannot be stated and the level can. Separately, a [court found statutory exclusions from birth registration unconstitutional](2026-07-29-timeslive-court-birth-registration-exclusions-unconstitutional) within the window, which goes to the same register from the entry end rather than the collection end.

summary: A simplified beneficial-ownership declaration [processed more than 23,000 filings in three weeks](2025-09-04-cipc-optimised-beneficial-ownership-declaration), a [partnership register was operationalised](2026-05-20-sars-beneficial-owner-register-partnership-it3bo), and [a bill would add deregistration for non-filing](2026-05-27-general-laws-amlctf-amendment-bill-b15-2026).
developments:
2025-08-22 — [a simplified online beneficial-ownership declaration entered service, with more than 23,000 declarations processed by the notice date three weeks later](2025-09-04-cipc-optimised-beneficial-ownership-declaration), against [the companies commission's own annual reporting](2026-03-01-cipc-annual-report-2024-25).

2026-05-20 — [the revenue service operationalised a structured partnership beneficial-owner register and filing workflow, generating persistent partnership and partner reference numbers for later validation and pre-population](2026-05-20-sars-beneficial-owner-register-partnership-it3bo). Two beneficial-ownership registers now run in parallel and no source states whether they reconcile.

2026-05-27 — [a bill was published requiring reporting of material beneficial-ownership discrepancies, deregistration after prolonged failure to file required registers, and tribunal review of administrative fines](2026-05-27-general-laws-amlctf-amendment-bill-b15-2026). It is the enforcement half of the two registers and it is not enacted.

progress: No change, the system established in the record for the first time
summary: The grant payment system [was confirmed in Parliament as administering payments to more than 18 million monthly beneficiaries](2025-07-01-parliamentary-question-nw3638-socpen).
developments:
2025-07-01 — [a ministerial reply confirmed the system administering grant payments to more than 18 million monthly beneficiaries](2025-07-01-parliamentary-question-nw3638-socpen). Nothing was held on it before, so what moved is the record rather than the register.

It is the largest beneficiary count of any system on this ledger by a wide margin, and the base holds no architecture, uptime, modernisation programme or replacement plan for it.

That absence is the finding. The systems this report describes as advancing — the biometric register, the exchange pilot, the verification portal — all assume a social protection register they can query, and the register itself appears in the record only as an answer to a parliamentary question.

summary: Voter registration [opened inside a messaging platform on 4 August 2026](2026-08-07-south-africa-whatsapp-voter-registration) and carried 1.7m transactions over the final weekend, with 291,016 first-time registrations.
developments:
2026-08-04 — the electoral commission [launched voter registration inside a messaging platform three days before the deadline for the November local elections](2026-08-07-south-africa-whatsapp-voter-registration), running one-time-password authentication, document upload, address verification and voting-station confirmation over it. [The final weekend carried 1.7m registration transactions and 291,016 first-time registrations, of which the online portal alone carried 238,000, and 46% of new registrations were by people under 29](2026-08-07-south-africa-whatsapp-voter-registration).

Two absences accompany the launch: no statement on data handling, and none on a fallback if the channel fails. A national register accepting enrolment through a private messaging platform, stood up three days before a deadline, is a delivery achievement and a dependency in the same act.

summary: The Tax Administration Act's 2026 amendment [enables a simplified express customs regime and a voluntary electronic value-added-tax reporting system](2026-04-01-tax-administration-laws-amendment-act-4-of-2026), and [a reference-number enquiry service is documented](2026-08-14-sars-tax-reference-number-enquiry-services-efiling).
developments:
[The Tax Administration Act of 2011 is the register's statutory basis](2012-07-04-tax-administration-act-28-of-2011). 2026-04-01 — [an amendment Act was enacted creating the enabling framework for a simplified customs regime for door-to-door express imports and exports and for a voluntary value-added-tax electronic reporting system](2026-04-01-tax-administration-laws-amendment-act-4-of-2026).

Voluntary is the operative word: the reporting system the amendment enables carries no obligation, no commencement date and no uptake figure on the record.

2026-08-14 — [a self-service channel for retrieving and verifying a taxpayer reference number is documented in an external guide](2026-08-14-sars-tax-reference-number-enquiry-services-efiling), a service guide rather than a service report, with no usage figure published.

summary: Sections of the deeds amendment [came into operation in September 2025](2025-09-01-deeds-registries-amendment-act-commencement-proclamation-286-2025) and [the fee schedule was replaced in February 2026](2026-02-27-deeds-registries-act-regulations-amendment-2026), on [a 2019 electronic registration statute](2019-09-19-electronic-deeds-registration-systems-act-19-of-2019).
developments:
[The Electronic Deeds Registration Systems Act of 2019 is the statute creating an electronic deeds register](2019-09-19-electronic-deeds-registration-systems-act-19-of-2019). 2025-09-01 — [named sections of the 2024 amendment came into operation](2025-09-01-deeds-registries-amendment-act-commencement-proclamation-286-2025), moving the amended registration framework into effect.

2026-02-27 — [the schedule of deeds office fees was replaced, setting a R52 lodgement fee and revised transfer-fee bands effective one month after publication](2026-02-27-deeds-registries-act-regulations-amendment-2026).

Seven years after the electronic statute, no source states how much of the register is actually electronic. The one piece of evidence that back-scanning had been completed anywhere came from a fire, reported under rural registry offices.

summary: The [national digital health strategy's term expired in 2024](2019-01-01-south-africa-national-digital-health-strategy-2019-2024) and no successor is held; nothing in the window replaces or reports against it.
developments:
The standing instrument is a [national digital health strategy for 2019 to 2024](2019-01-01-south-africa-national-digital-health-strategy-2019-2024), whose term has expired with no successor on the base. It set nine strategic interventions, proposed a national grant for digital health targeting three to five per cent of health expenditure, and committed to a master patient index for all South Africans, conformance testing of all health information systems and a review of digital-health governance by 2020.

The base holds nothing measuring what any of it delivered, and nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 replaces it. A strategy two years past its term, with no successor and no evaluation, is the position — and the interoperability architecture reported separately under health systems is doing the work a current strategy would otherwise carry.

summary: The student funding scheme was [placed under administration with ICT named its largest operational risk](2026-08-07-nsfas-says-ict-is-its-biggest-operational-risk) — fragmented, manual and not fit for purpose, on the administrator's own words.
developments:
2026-08-07 — the administrator's stabilisation plan [states that ICT is the scheme's biggest operational risk, as it is fragmented, manual and not fit for purpose](2026-08-07-nsfas-says-ict-is-its-biggest-operational-risk). The same submission reports 66 major audit findings and a disclaimer audit opinion, 115 overdue internal audit findings and nine material irregularities, five of them data or systems defects. The scheme was placed under administration in May 2026, its board having been dissolved in 2024 over IT-system failures, and the governance failures were referred for investigation.

At provincial level a longer-standing system held its position: [online school admissions for the 2027 intake opened on 5 August 2026](2026-08-05-gauteng-2027-online-school-admissions), a system running since 2016 that carries a documented record of concurrency failures under load, learners unplaced at the start of the academic year and manipulation by officials, with a better system framed as a future intention.

progress: Mixed, verification widened while access narrowed
summary: [420,000 grants were flagged and roughly 160,000 recipients did not complete review](2026-07-31-sa-child-grant-reviews-leave-mothers-stranded-sassa), with [child-grant recipients reporting months without payment](2026-07-30-timeslive-sassa-fraud-crackdown-delays-payments).
developments:
2026-07 — review scope widened and access narrowed in the same movement. [Some 420,000 grants were flagged during 2025/26 and roughly 160,000 beneficiaries did not complete the review](2026-07-31-sa-child-grant-reviews-leave-mothers-stranded-sassa), with child-grant recipients reporting months without payment; the [same crackdown is reported as delaying payments](2026-07-30-timeslive-sassa-fraud-crackdown-delays-payments).

The mechanism that would settle whether any of this is lawful was neither implemented nor decided inside the window: a [bank-account means test applied across eight grants is under appeal, with a hearing on 25 August 2026](2026-07-25-sa-digital-profiteers-part-one-digitalised-grants-system).

A verification programme is doing what it was built to do and a sixth of those it touched fell out of payment while it did. Both halves are on the record and neither is disputed, which is why this row is Mixed rather than either one of them.

summary: The courts digitisation project was [referred to the special investigating unit after the contractor denied the department access to its own records](2026-08-13-south-africa-courts-digitisation-siu-hawks-referral).
developments:
2026-08-13 — the justice minister [referred the courts digitisation project to the special investigating unit and the police priority crimes unit after the contractor denied the department access to its own records at the Master of the High Court in Pretoria](2026-08-13-south-africa-courts-digitisation-siu-hawks-referral). Records storage has been outsourced to that contractor since 2021 across three provinces.

No contract value, term, custody arrangement or data-protection provision for the outsourced court records is held. A department locked out of its own records is a custody failure before it is a procurement one, and it is the sharpest instance on this ledger of the state holding neither the system nor the data it depends on.

summary: A [modernisation programme was announced in April 2026](2026-07-23-pwc-ten-insights-into-4ir-south-african-mining-2026); the base holds no scope, budget or delivery date for it, only a second-hand account.
developments:
2026-04 — a revenue service modernisation programme [was announced](2026-07-23-pwc-ten-insights-into-4ir-south-african-mining-2026), reaching the base only through a professional services firm's sector report rather than through the service's own publication.

That is the whole of what is held: no scope statement, budget, delivery date or architecture. What is better evidenced is the automation inside the existing system, reported under artificial intelligence in government administration, and the VAT design work reported under revenue collection — so the tax estate is moving in two documented places and the programme said to contain them is not documented at all.

summary: The revenue service convened five administrations on a joint customs data-exchange roadmap ([roadmap](2026-08-31-farmersreviewafrica-southern-african-customs-administrations-agree-roadmap-for-faster)).
developments:
The South African Revenue Service hosted and five southern African customs administrations adopted a joint roadmap and action plan for customs-to-customs data exchange in Pretoria on 24-26 August 2026 ([roadmap](2026-08-31-farmersreviewafrica-southern-african-customs-administrations-agree-roadmap-for-faster)).

This puts South Africa's customs system at the centre of a regional exchange design rather than a single bilateral link.

The base holds no measure of the domestic customs system's own performance — clearance times, declaration volumes or the share processed without intervention.

summary: A mining cadastre pilot [was reported complete to Parliament](2025-11-25-parliament-mining-cadastre-system-pilot), and [a geospatial information strategy reached its first provincial roadshow](2026-05-20-gims-provincial-roadshow-speech-mohai).
developments:
2025-11-25 — [the provincial pilot of the mining cadastre was reported complete to Parliament, a spatially defined rights register intended to improve the digital administration and transparency of mining licensing](2025-11-25-parliament-mining-cadastre-system-pilot). No national rollout date, cost or licence-volume figure is published.

2026-05-20 — [the Geospatial Information Management Strategy moved toward implementation at its first provincial roadshow, with a live geospatial dashboard demonstrated and work under way with one province and one metro on spatial data governance and interoperability](2026-05-20-gims-provincial-roadshow-speech-mohai).

Beneath both, [land administration and spatial systems are carried as departmental commitments in the annual performance plan](2026-03-30-dlrrd-annual-performance-plan-2026-27), held as an excerpt with no system named, and [an annual report records the state of the deeds and cadastral estate](2024-09-30-dalrrd-annual-report-2023-24).

summary: The single citizen application [reached a production-ready pilot with a stable platform due September 2026](2026-08-03-itweb-mymzansi-production-ready-vulindlela-q1), and the [electronic travel authorisation went live at four airports](2026-08-13-south-africa-eta-digital-travel-four-airports).
developments:
2026-08-03 — the single citizen application [progressed from proof of concept to a production-ready pilot with governance arrangements in place](2026-08-03-itweb-mymzansi-production-ready-vulindlela-q1), with the stable platform, the first credential use case and a shared government platform all targeted for September 2026 and further departmental use cases for March 2027. Public access had been promised for the first half of 2026 in [the February 2026 address](2026-02-13-sona-2026-digital-mega-platform), so the platform advanced and its date slipped in the same window. The first credential is a digital school-leaving certificate, in testing with the certifying body.

2026-08-12/16 — the [electronic travel authorisation went live at four airports and was launched by the President](2026-08-13-south-africa-eta-digital-travel-four-airports), [with full visa-type rollout targeted by end-2026](2026-08-16-politicsweb-ramaphosa-electronic-travel-authorisation-launch). The department publishes no statistical series for it and the bases do not reconcile: 88,033 applications to January 2026 in a parliamentary reply, [over 75,000 processed with nearly 4,500 rejections at the May budget vote](2026-05-15-schreiber-home-affairs-budget-vote-2026-27-speech), 203,000 processed by July, and 6,126 rejections put at 2.8% of pilot submissions in August.

The social security agency opened a messaging self-service channel for grant application, review and proof-of-life status, after verification by mobile number, one-time PIN and identity number ([channel](2026-08-28-citizen-za-sassa-whatsapp-self-service)).

progress: Advanced, both instances provincial rather than local
summary: A province [launched an AI-evaluated infrastructure platform](2026-07-31-inaugural-western-cape-infrastructure-ministerial-roundtable-a-rousing-success) and [opened a funding-matching platform to small business](2026-08-12-western-cape-finfind-digital-funding-platform); no municipal-level system is on the ledger.
developments:
2026-07-30 — a provincial government [launched an infrastructure platform that evaluates projects automatically against treasury rules and a quality standard via an AI agent](2026-07-31-inaugural-western-cape-infrastructure-ministerial-roundtable-a-rousing-success), reporting an evaluated pipeline of 52 projects worth R132bn with 11 worth over R20bn to be released to market, and memoranda signed with four national and academic bodies.

2026-08-12 — the same province [opened free access for small and medium enterprises to a matching platform covering over 300 funders and 600 finance products](2026-08-12-western-cape-finfind-digital-funding-platform). The platform is a private one and the counts are its own; [the same data put 65.3% of provincial applicants as unable to supply their latest financial statements](2026-08-12-western-cape-finfind-digital-funding-platform), which says more about the constraint than the platform does.

Both are provincial. The base holds no municipal ICT system, no municipal ICT expenditure data and no local-government digitisation programme at all, so what is advancing sits one tier above the one this indicator asks about.

The third instance is local rather than provincial: an appointment-only home affairs office opened inside the Cape Town Civic Centre on 24 August 2026, the first municipal facility to host one ([office](2026-08-24-timeslive-cape-town-home-affairs-queue)).

summary: One metro [reported a records digitisation programme to the National Council of Provinces](2025-11-21-mangaung-digital-transformation-programme-status) and [another awarded an electronic records system](2026-01-09-emfuleni-procurement-plan-reporting-q2-2025-26), under [standing national archives guidance](2026-08-26-narssa-managing-electronic-records-guidance-page).
developments:
2025-11-21 — [a metro reported its technology roadmap, document-management rollout and digitisation of hard-copy and historical municipal records to the National Council of Provinces, naming budget, legacy-system and skills constraints](2025-11-21-mangaung-digital-transformation-programme-status). A municipality naming its own constraints is rarer on this ledger than the programme itself.

2026-01-09 — [a second municipality recorded the award of an in-house server-based electronic records-management system on a three-year term from October 2025](2026-01-09-emfuleni-procurement-plan-reporting-q2-2025-26), known only through a procurement annexure, so the award is established and the deployment is not.

[The national archives publishes standing guidance on managing electronic records](2026-08-26-narssa-managing-electronic-records-guidance-page), which is the rule set both are obliged to work to, and no compliance assessment against it appears for any municipality.

The local government association [issued a request for proposal for consultants to build a municipal revenue management plan across the 257 municipalities it represents, putting consumer debt at about R467.2bn, municipalities' own debt to creditors at about R160.8bn and annual water and electricity revenue loss at about R25bn](2026-08-24-timeslive-salga-municipal-billing-digitisation). Unverified indigent registers and data deficiencies are named among the losses the consultants are to identify.

summary: Implementation partners [were invited to deploy the electronic medical record across eight provinces](2026-03-03-ndoh-emr-digital-solution-implementation-invitation-to-bid), with [one province already recognised for a primary-care deployment](2026-05-14-free-state-health-emr-primary-health-care-award).
developments:
2026-03-03 — [public-health service providers were invited to implement the electronic medical record solution across eight provinces](2026-03-03-ndoh-emr-digital-solution-implementation-invitation-to-bid), held as an excerpt with no award, value or facility count on file.

2026-05-14 — [one province deployed an electronic medical record across primary health care, with training, connectivity, cybersecurity and interoperability recorded as outstanding work](2026-05-14-free-state-health-emr-primary-health-care-award). The outstanding list is the useful part: the record is installed and the conditions for using it are not met.

[The national department carries a chief directorate for health systems digital information](2026-08-26-ndoh-chief-directorate-health-systems-digital-information) as the standing owner, on an undated page with no facility or coverage figure.

summary: A provincial treasury [launched a digital access programme for rural and under-resourced schools](2026-04-14-kzn-digital-access-programme-launch), and [an off-grid containerised media lab entered service at one primary school](2026-05-29-peter-mokaba-primary-school-media-lab-handover).
developments:
2026-04-14 — [a provincial treasury launched a Digital Access Programme for rural and under-resourced schools in one district, with announced expansion to two further districts](2026-04-14-kzn-digital-access-programme-launch). No school count, budget or device figure is published, and [the national digital education strategy of September 2025 is the policy frame it sits under](2025-09-16-dbe-digital-education-strategy).

2026-05-29 — [a containerised off-grid media lab entered service at one primary school, with solar generation and battery storage, offering coding and robotics training to surrounding schools](2026-05-29-peter-mokaba-primary-school-media-lab-handover).

The off-grid design is the notable part. Against the rural electrification position reported under energy, a school computer laboratory that generates its own power is a workaround for a constraint the education programmes cannot themselves remove.

summary: All paper land records at one regional deeds registry [had already been back-scanned when the building burned](2026-03-26-new-location-for-mthatha-deeds-office-after-fire), carrying service to a new location.
developments:
2026-03-26 — [all paper records of registered land at one regional deeds registry had already been back-scanned into the electronic deeds system when the building burned, carrying service continuity to a new location](2026-03-26-new-location-for-mthatha-deeds-office-after-fire).

It is the clearest evidence on this ledger that back-scanning of a regional registry had actually been completed, and it is evidenced by a fire rather than by a programme report. Nothing else states how many registries have been converted, or on what schedule.

The wider office estate is reported only in aggregate: [the home affairs annual report is held as an excerpt](2025-09-01-department-of-home-affairs-annual-report-2024-25) and carries no rural office count on the record.

summary: Police gave Parliament [the count of sites with integrated person management as at March 2026](2026-04-30-ncop-question-331-integrated-person-management-sites), naming connectivity, rugged devices and scanners as the constraints.
developments:
2026-04-30 — [the count of police sites with integrated person management implemented was given to Parliament as at 31 March 2026, with personnel, connectivity, rugged devices and scanners named as the dependencies for wider rollout](2026-04-30-ncop-question-331-integrated-person-management-sites).

2026-06-03 — [Parliament recorded station hardware and network rollout counts and an electronic policing policy directing digital docket management into pilot stations](2026-06-03-select-committee-report-saps-budget-vote-28-2026-27).

The dependencies named are physical rather than software — power, connection, devices — which is what makes rural stations the binding case rather than an afterthought. [The national rural safety strategy is the standing policy frame](2019-04-01-national-rural-safety-strategy) and predates all of it.

progress: Advanced, and ahead of any rule governing it
summary: A [public-service chatbot launched on 31 July 2026](2026-08-01-innovation-meets-impact-as-minister-buthelezi-launches-batho-pele-ai-chatbot), the revenue service [automates all verifications and 88.41% of complex audits](2026-07-27-sars-ai-machine-learning-tax-compliance), and [travel screening by machine learning is intended](2026-08-11-techcabal-south-africa-machine-learning-border-checks).
developments:
2026-07-31 — the public service department [launched a citizen and public-servant chatbot built on an open-weight model family under a partnership with the model's owner and a local supplier](2026-08-01-innovation-meets-impact-as-minister-buthelezi-launches-batho-pele-ai-chatbot), providing policy, circular and legislation lookups in nine official languages, explicitly decision-support with no decision-making authority.

2026-07-27 — the revenue service [reports automated selection covering 100% of verifications and 88.41% of complex audits](2026-07-27-sars-ai-machine-learning-tax-compliance). At the border, [85% of travel-authorisation applications are assessed automatically against a 24-hour target and 40 document-authenticity parameters](2026-08-13-south-africa-eta-digital-travel-four-airports), with no appeal route, accuracy rate, disparate-impact testing or human-review threshold stated. The department has [stated an intention to screen travellers for fraud using machine learning](2026-08-11-techcabal-south-africa-machine-learning-border-checks), with no system, procurement, legal basis or accuracy measure published.

Automated decision-making expanded through the whole period without a governing framework, and the only test of it is the litigation reported under AI legislation.

progress: Advanced, on the banks' own figures
summary: One bank reports [over 39,000 staff, 72% of its workforce, as active generative-AI users](2026-08-17-standard-bank-ai-enabled-organisation); another, [a chatbot handling over 100,000 queries a month from about 1.6 million users](2026-08-20-itweb-absa-ai-chatbot-1-6m-users).
developments:
2026-08-17 — a large bank [reported more than 39,000 staff, 72% of its workforce, as active generative-AI users on a multi-model enterprise platform hosted on a foreign cloud provider](2026-08-17-standard-bank-ai-enabled-organisation), naming relationship management, servicing, payments and lending as priority areas.

2026-08-20 — a different institution [reported an agentic chatbot handling over 100,000 queries a month from about 1.6 million users in the first half of 2026](2026-08-20-itweb-absa-ai-chatbot-1-6m-users), alongside 30,000 employees a month on a vendor productivity assistant, more than 3,800 staff-built automation agents in production and over 1,400 developers on AI-assisted coding tools.

The two are separate institutions and are not comparable with each other. Both are the banks' own figures for adoption, not for automated decisions or customer-facing outcomes, and neither states a model inventory, an assurance process or any customer disclosure. The country holds no AI incident or assurance register against which any of it could be checked.

summary: A distributed national research network in artificial intelligence [is the country's standing public capability](2026-08-26-cair-structure-and-history), with no funding, headcount or output figure published.
developments:
[A distributed national research network in artificial intelligence is hosted across universities with a national coordinating centre](2026-08-26-cair-structure-and-history), the standing public research capability in the field. The page is undated and carries no funding, headcount or output figure.

Nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 changes it: no national model, dataset or system built in the country appears on this ledger, and the compute that would host one is reported under data storage as expanding for commercial tenants rather than for research.

[A comparative study of national artificial-intelligence strategies places the country's policy position](2026-01-01-world-bank-radu-global-landscape-national-ai-strategies) rather than its research base, and the policy itself was withdrawn, reported under strategy.

progress: Advanced, supervisory practice moving ahead of any published framework
summary: The medicines regulator [requires every AI-enabled device to be authorised before use](2025-09-26-sahpra-regulatory-requirements-ai-ml-enabled-medical-devices), and the prudential authority [has embedded AI into bank supervision](2026-07-16-banks-stricter-ai-scrutiny-regulator) with a framework only expected.
developments:
2025-09-26 — the medicines regulator [issued requirements for AI and machine-learning enabled medical devices](2025-09-26-sahpra-regulatory-requirements-ai-ml-enabled-medical-devices): every such device must be authorised before use and its importer or manufacturer licensed, with higher-class applicants required to produce prior approval from a reference jurisdiction or international prequalification plus local clinical evidence including subgroup analysis by sex, age and ethnicity. It also states that product registration has not commenced, that AI-specific pathways are still to be developed, and that it awaits international guidance before adopting predetermined change-control plans — so the rule exists and the gate it describes is not yet open.

2026-07-16 — in finance, [supervision moved before rulemaking](2026-07-16-banks-stricter-ai-scrutiny-regulator): the prudential authority's annual report embeds AI, cloud, cyber and data-offshoring into bank supervision and ran a first nationwide AI-adoption survey, naming regulatory uncertainty, AI skills and governance as the barriers. A [dedicated AI-in-finance regulatory framework is expected within 2026](2026-01-30 2026 fintech year ahead) and is not published.

progress: Mixed, operators and a data product advanced while the sector's transformation council was found dysfunctional
summary: The third operator [reported R12.64bn revenue and R4.16bn profit](2026-08-24-cell-c-fy26-results-techafricanews), while the sector's B-BBEE council [had its chair replaced after being found dysfunctional](2026-08-14-ict-sector-council-chairperson-gets-the-boot).
developments:
2026-08-24 — the third mobile operator [reported R12.64bn revenue and R4.16bn profit after tax for the year to 31 May 2026, a prepaid base past 8 million and a wholesale virtual-operator base of 5.71 million](2026-08-24-cell-c-fy26-results-techafricanews). It runs an asset-light model on other operators' radio networks, so the growth is a virtual-operator business rather than network build — as its [5G service, live from 21 August 2026, makes plain: it claims the widest coverage in the country by roaming on both larger operators' sites rather than owning radio infrastructure](2026-08-21-techcentral-cell-c-5g-launch).

2026-08-19 — a listed payments company [consolidated a division selling near-real-time item-level intelligence on the informal retail economy, drawn from a point-of-sale network of over 90,000 spaza shops and taverns and 10,500 checkouts](2026-08-19-itweb-lesaka-data-insights-spaza-economy). The network figures are the company's own, and no consent basis, pricing or data-protection assessment for reselling merchant transaction data is stated.

2026-08-14 — against both, the minister [replaced the ICT sector transformation council's chairperson after a departmental investigation found the council dysfunctional](2026-08-14-ict-sector-council-chairperson-gets-the-boot). The investigation report is not published and no remedial plan or date for a permanent appointment is stated.

summary: Two centres opened in the window — [a continental digital transformation centre with the ITU](2026-03-06-african-digital-transformation-centre-launch) and [an industry and technology centre hosted by a university](2025-09-22-south-african-centre-for-industry-and-technology-launch).
developments:
2026-03-06 — [the African Digital Transformation Centre opened at an innovation hub in the capital, established with the International Telecommunication Union as part of its network of acceleration centres, to support technology small enterprises and digital entrepreneurs across the continent](2026-03-06-african-digital-transformation-centre-launch).

2025-09-22 — [a South African Centre for Industry and Technology was launched, hosted by a university in partnership with an international forum and opened alongside a G20 research and innovation ministerial](2025-09-22-south-african-centre-for-industry-and-technology-launch).

Beneath both, [the small business department runs a standing network of incubation and digital hubs](2026-08-26-dsbd-incubation-and-digital-hubs), on an undated page with no hub count, spend or enterprise figure.

Two openings in a year and no occupancy, cohort or funding figure for any of them is the pattern: hubs are announced here and their output is not measured.

summary: Venture funding fell from [$335.9m across 42 ventures in 2025, leading the continent](2026-02-27 SA powers Africa's $1.64bn tech funding rebound), to [fourth place at $83m in the first half of 2026](2026-07-27-african-vc-h1-2026-concentration-early-stage-thinning).
developments:
Funding reversed inside the window. The country [raised $335.9m across 42 ventures in calendar 2025 on a measure its publisher describes as a minimum floor, leading the continent](2026-02-27 SA powers Africa's $1.64bn tech funding rebound).

2026-07-27 — in the first half of 2026 it [ranked fourth at $83m, as continental deal count fell 42% year on year and early-stage activity thinned](2026-07-27-african-vc-h1-2026-concentration-early-stage-thinning).

The two halves are not strictly comparable — a full year against a half — but the ranking is, and first to fourth on the continent in six months is the finding. No domestic count of hubs, incubators, registrations or exits appears on this ledger to set against it, so the only visible measure of the startup base is the money going into it.

summary: The public service department [tendered in August 2026 to build a training programme for departmental information security officers](2026-08-17-dpsa-ict-tenders-info-security-training) across the public sector.
developments:
2026-08-17 — the public service and administration department [put out to tender the construction of a training programme for departmental information security officers across the public sector](2026-08-17-dpsa-ict-tenders-info-security-training), to implement the directive on public service information security.

No officer count, curriculum, budget or compliance deadline under that directive is stated, so what the tender implies about the current state — that the officers exist and the training does not — is the most it can be read to say. It is the only civil-service digital capability instrument anywhere on this ledger, and it addresses one specialist role rather than the service's general digital literacy.

progress: Advanced, on access centres, with literacy itself unmeasured
summary: A province [opened its 83rd public access centre](2026-06-11-western-cape-rheenendal-ecentre-opening), while the only demand-side survey the base holds [is two years old](2024-05-01-after-access-2022-23-south-africa-report).
developments:
2026-06-11 — [a province opened its 83rd brick-and-mortar public access centre, adding a business corner, public access centre and training centre to a network also served by a mobile unit](2026-06-11-western-cape-rheenendal-ecentre-opening). No user, training or throughput figure is published for the network.

[The one nationally representative demand-side survey the base holds covers household and individual access, use and affordability](2024-05-01-after-access-2022-23-south-africa-report), held as an excerpt and two years old at the window's close.

No digital-literacy or digital-skills rate is measured in it or anywhere else on this ledger. So the country is building places to go online and has no measurement of whether the people using them can.

summary: A vendor academy and a provincial education department [agreed to take networking, cyber security and AI courses into 235 schools from February 2027](2026-08-18-cisco-hanley-digital-skills-northern-cape).
developments:
2026-08-18 — a networking vendor's academy and a private group [agreed with a provincial education department to take networking, cyber security and artificial-intelligence courses into 235 schools](2026-08-18-cisco-hanley-digital-skills-northern-cape), as extracurricular classes for grades 10 to 12 beginning February 2027, inside a global programme the vendor states has trained more than 600,000 South Africans.

It is announced for a start five months beyond this window's close. No learner target, cost, funding split, teacher-training provision or certification pathway is published, and [the 600,000 is the vendor's own figure](2026-08-18-cisco-hanley-digital-skills-northern-cape). Extracurricular classes delivered by a vendor in one province is what the base holds on this indicator, and there is no national curriculum instrument beside it.

summary: University research [finds AI adoption in teaching and assessment outpacing institutional policy](2026-08-17-ai-adoption-higher-education-policy-gaps-sa), with lecturers reporting inconsistent or absent guidance and no sector instrument held.
developments:
2026-08-17 — research from a South African university [finds artificial-intelligence adoption in teaching and assessment outpacing institutional policy](2026-08-17-ai-adoption-higher-education-policy-gaps-sa), with lecturers reporting inconsistent or absent guidance on accountability, on the reliability of detection tools and on academic integrity.

No sector-wide instrument and no regulator guidance is held, and nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 produces one. What the base holds on university capability is therefore a finding about the absence of governance rather than any measure of facilities, enrolment or qualifications — which are not on this ledger at all.

progress: Mixed, the delivery programmes moved and the national strategy did not
summary: A skills fund [went to year-round applications with 97% of 1,800 participants absorbed into employment](2026-08-25-collective-x-digital-skills-impact-fund), while the [2020 national strategy is under review with no replacement](2026-07-23-sa-parliamentary-question-nw3567-ai-labour-market-dcdt).
developments:
2026-08-25 — a R200m skills fund [dropped its fixed application windows for year-round applications, having taken more than 1,800 young people across all nine provinces, 97% of them absorbed into employment and over 75% still employed after six months](2026-08-25-collective-x-digital-skills-impact-fund), against operator targets of 40,000 digitally skilled workers a year by 2030.

2026-07-23 — the strategy did not move: the [2020 national digital and future skills strategy is under comprehensive review with no replacement](2026-07-23-sa-parliamentary-question-nw3567-ai-labour-market-dcdt), disclosed in a written parliamentary reply rather than announced, alongside a national competency framework still in development. The department declined to forecast artificial intelligence's net employment effect.

2026-07-22 — and the institution that funds sector skills [was referred for a governance assessment](2026-07-22-mict-seta-governance-referred-to-skills-authority).

The measurement of the gap is now better than the response to it. Employers report [about 7% of ICT and engineering posts unfilled, with software developers, network engineers and security specialists hardest to fill, and attribute the gap 26% to basic-level training, 24% to graduate pipeline throughput and 21% to the pace of technological change](2026-06-24-world-bank-south-africa-digital-skills-pipeline-full-report), in a [development bank report produced with the higher education department](2026-08-14-world-bank-mastercard-foundation-south-africa-digital-skills).

progress: No change, first measured in this window with nothing before it to compare
summary: The country places [18th worldwide and is the only African country in the top 20 for digital-privacy research output](2026-08-18-sajim-privacy-vulnerable-populations-bibliometric), on a review of 4,760 articles from 2005 to 2025.
developments:
2026-08-18 — a bibliometric analysis of [4,760 articles over twenty years places the country 18th worldwide and the only African country in the top 20 for digital-privacy research output](2026-08-18-sajim-privacy-vulnerable-populations-bibliometric). It is the one place on this ledger where the country ranks near the top of anything.

Two qualifications carried by the same review. It measures volume of output, not the coverage of the populations most exposed — refugees, people with disabilities, older people and racial and ethnic minorities are found notably underrepresented in that literature. And it is a first measurement here, with no earlier standing on the base to compare, so the level is stated and the direction is not.

What the base does not hold is any link from that research capacity to policy: no research council submission, advisory panel or commissioned study appears in the instruments recorded elsewhere in this report.

summary: A province [launched a road-defect reporting application that routes each report to the responsible authority](2026-03-04-western-cape-roads4u-app-launch), and [a municipality launched a service-request channel](2026-03-02-hessequa-collab-citizen-app-launch).
developments:
2026-03-04 — [a road-defect reporting application launched, geolocating each report and routing it to the responsible road authority, issuing reference numbers and status updates to the reporter](2026-03-04-western-cape-roads4u-app-launch). The routing and the reference number are what distinguish it from a complaints inbox, and no volume figure is published.

2026-03-02 — [a municipality launched a digital service-reporting channel letting residents log and track requests and receive municipal updates](2026-03-02-hessequa-collab-citizen-app-launch).

Both are sub-national and both arrived in the same week. No national feedback channel appears on this ledger, and neither publishes a resolution rate — which is the measure that separates a reporting channel from a service.

summary: A civil-society coalition [asked the rights commission to halt data-centre developments pending transparent public participation](2026-08-11-south-africa-climate-justice-coalition-data-centre-participation); no participation process or commission response is on record.
developments:
2026-08-10 — a climate justice coalition [submitted concerns to the human rights commission calling for a halt on data-centre developments pending transparent public participation](2026-08-11-south-africa-climate-justice-coalition-data-centre-participation), citing strain on scarce water, land and electricity. No participation process, commission response or moratorium is on record.

The route it took is the finding. There is no statutory participation step for these approvals to attach to, so the objection was lodged with a rights body rather than a planning or energy regulator, and it arrived alongside the [commission's own call for submissions](2026-05-22-sahrc-call-for-submissions-data-centres-human-rights). Participation happening through a human rights complaint is a description of what the ordinary process does not provide.

summary: The gender equality commission [announced a national study on women's participation in the digital economy](2026-03-19-cge-digital-gender-transformation-national-study-media-statement), aimed at policy recommendations to close the access gap.
developments:
2026-03-19 — [a national study on digital gender transformation was announced by the gender equality commission, on women's participation in the digital economy and aimed at producing gender-responsive policy recommendations to close the digital access gap](2026-03-19-cge-digital-gender-transformation-national-study-media-statement). Nothing of the kind existed on this ledger before it.

The standing instrument beside it is [a framework on gender-responsive planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and auditing](2024-02-01-gender-responsive-planning-budgeting-monitoring-evaluation-auditing-framework), which is a budgeting method rather than a digital measure.

No sex-disaggregated access, use or skills figure appears anywhere on this ledger, so the study would be measuring something the country has never published.

summary: A [seven-point plan on disability-inclusive data, universal design and AI-enabled assistive technology was agreed on 12 August 2026](2026-08-12-south-africa-china-disability-inclusion-data-cooperation), anchored in a proposed centre of excellence.
developments:
2026-08-12 — a [seven-point plan was agreed with a bilateral partner to deepen cooperation on disability-inclusive data, universal design and artificial-intelligence-enabled assistive technology](2026-08-12-south-africa-china-disability-inclusion-data-cooperation), anchored in a proposed disability centre of excellence working with the national statistics office.

No instrument, funding, timetable or data-sharing arrangement is published for cooperation that names the national statistics office as a partner, which is the gap worth naming: an agreement about disability data with a foreign partner, and no domestic statement of what data would be collected, held or shared. It is also the only disability-related digital instrument on this ledger.

summary: A bill [would extend employment services to foreign nationals, refugees and asylum seekers, with work-authorisation verification](2026-05-29-employment-services-amendment-bill-b16-2026).
developments:
2026-05-29 — [a bill was published extending the statutory employment-services framework to foreign nationals, refugees and asylum seekers, creating work-authorisation verification and requiring a framework for collecting information on their recruitment and employment](2026-05-29-employment-services-amendment-bill-b16-2026), against [the standing refugees statute of 1998](1998-12-02-refugees-act-130-of-1998).

The verification duty is the part that touches this report: it would run against the identity layer, and nothing states how a person without a South African identity number is verified, or what record is kept of the check.

It is a bill. No enactment, commencement or implementing system appears, and the white paper reported under digital identity carries the same population without stating how they are registered.

progress: Mixed, household telephone access is now near-universal while the zero-rating obligation owed since 2022 is running late
summary: Households with no telephone fell to 3.7% in 2025 from nearly 55% in 2002 ([figures](2026-08-28-mobile-penetration-groundup)), while the zero-rating obligation runs late ([acknowledgement](2026-08-27-zero-rating-public-benefit-sites-businessday)).
developments:
The share of households with no telephone at all fell from nearly 55% in 2002 to 3.7% — about 740,000 households — in 2025, with 93.8% holding a cellphone only and 2.5% holding both a cellphone and a landline ([figures](2026-08-28-mobile-penetration-groundup)).

The communications minister acknowledged on 27 August 2026 that the zero-rating of public-benefit websites owed under the 2022 spectrum auction is moving slowly, five months before its deadline, while saying he remains confident it will be met ([acknowledgement](2026-08-27-zero-rating-public-benefit-sites-businessday)).

Device access and affordable access are different problems, and the base's evidence now separates them: near-universal handset ownership alongside an unmet obligation to make public-interest content free to reach.

summary: The statistics office [achieved 399 of 414 targets and built an integrated indicator framework](2026-06-23-parliament-atc-109-2026), against a 23% vacancy rate and an R2.2 billion shortfall.
developments:
2026-06-23 — [399 of 414 targets were achieved for 2025/26 and an integrated indicator framework was built linking indicators to the national development plan, against a 23% vacancy rate and an R2.2 billion funding shortfall](2026-06-23-parliament-atc-109-2026), [on a published work programme for the year](2026-01-01-stats-sa-work-programme-2026-27).

It is the nearest thing to a national statistical development strategy the base holds, and the shortfall is stated by the office itself rather than by a critic.

A near-complete target achievement rate reported alongside a quarter of posts vacant and a two-billion-rand gap is the sort of pairing this frame exists to show: the delivery figure and the capacity figure point in opposite directions and both are official.

summary: The 2022 census [counted 62,027,503 people in the country's first digital census](2023-10-10-census-2022-statistical-release), and [a continuous population survey is being built to carry the interval between censuses](2026-08-26-cps-hspr-frame-update).
developments:
[The 2022 census was the country's fourth post-1994 census and its first conducted digitally, counting a population of 62,027,503](2023-10-10-census-2022-statistical-release). It is three years old at the window's close.

[A frame update was published for the continuous population survey and household survey programme redesign](2026-08-26-cps-hspr-frame-update), the instrument intended to carry population statistics between censuses. The page is undated and no first release is named.

The running series beside it is the labour force survey, which [put unemployment at 33.6% in the second quarter of 2026 and recorded questionnaire updates intended to keep the statistics internationally comparable](2026-08-11-quarterly-labour-force-survey-q2-2026).

summary: An insolvencies series [was restored after five years, its administrative supply having been cut off by a cyber incident](2026-07-21-data-on-insolvencies-now-available), and [index methods built on customs records were published](2026-03-19-export-and-import-unit-value-indices-sources-and-methods).
developments:
2026-07-21 — [the monthly insolvencies series was restored, having been interrupted since a 2021 cyber incident at the justice department cut off the administrative supply, with a first release covering June 2026 and a time series back to January 2023](2026-07-21-data-on-insolvencies-now-available).

That is the clearest cost of a security failure anywhere on this ledger: an official statistical series lost for five years because another department's systems went down, and recovered only now.

2026-03-19 — [the export and import unit value indices had their basket and weights revised effective with the January 2026 index, a series built from customs administrative records](2026-03-19-export-and-import-unit-value-indices-sources-and-methods), and [sources and methods were published for the residential property price index](2026-06-04-residential-property-price-index-sources-and-methods). Both depend on another agency's systems continuing to supply them.

progress: Advanced, a national map built and not published
summary: A [national broadband map was launched on 31 March 2026](2026-03-31 SA finally has a broadband map - and it reveals where the gaps are) and is recorded as not public, so the gaps it reveals are visible to its holders and not to anyone else.
developments:
2026-03-31 — a [national broadband map was launched](2026-03-31 SA finally has a broadband map - and it reveals where the gaps are), the first the country has held, and the ledger records it as implemented but not public.

That combination is the whole of the finding. A map that identifies where coverage is absent is the input every subsequent decision needs — the connectivity programmes, the spectrum release, the rapid-deployment by-law reported elsewhere in this report — and none of those decisions can be scrutinised against it while it stays closed. The regulator's [draft infrastructure database would compel operators to submit geo-referenced passive-infrastructure data twice a year](2026-04-12 Icasa moves to mandate national infrastructure database), which would deepen the same holding without changing who can see it.

The one open instrument on the ledger is narrower: an [open science policy](2026-03-01-south-african-open-science-policy) covering publicly funded research output, with no commencement date stated.

summary: A satellite maize monitoring system [entered use in two provinces, pushing dashboards and text alerts in local languages](2026-01-21-geomaize-satellite-crop-monitoring), and [imagery buying was centralised](2026-02-11-sansa-centralised-satellite-imagery-procurement).
developments:
2026-01-21 — [a satellite-based maize monitoring system entered use in two provinces, combining optical and thermal imagery with machine-learning models to push farmer dashboards and text alerts in local languages](2026-01-21-geomaize-satellite-crop-monitoring). It is the only satellite product on this ledger that reaches an end user directly, and the local-language text channel is what makes that possible. No user or hectare figure is published.

[The agricultural research council's earth observation unit is the standing capability behind it](2026-08-26-arc-iscw-earth-observation).

2026-02-11 — [government satellite-imagery buying moved to a coordinated multi-user licensing model run by the science department and the space agency, with an estimated saving of about R88 million against fragmented purchasing and agriculture among the participating portfolios](2026-02-11-sansa-centralised-satellite-imagery-procurement). The saving is the agency's own estimate.

summary: A continental meteorological satellite facility [was inaugurated in May 2026](2026-06-02-amsaf-inauguration), operationalising satellite-derived nowcasting and impact-based forecasting.
developments:
2026-05-18 — [the African Meteorological Satellite Application Facility was inaugurated under a European-funded project, operationalising satellite-derived nowcasting and impact-based forecasting for African meteorological services](2026-06-02-amsaf-inauguration).

2026-07-02 — [renewed African cooperation agreements were approved supporting infrastructure and uptake of third-generation meteorological satellite data across the continent](2026-07-02-eumetsat-strengthens-cooperation-with-africa), building on [an established regional approach to nowcasting in southern Africa](2022-03-01-regional-approach-to-nowcasting-southern-africa).

It is a continental facility with South African participation. No domestic user count, forecast product or warning issued through it is named, so what the record establishes is the capability rather than its use.

summary: The state's [public-service chatbot runs on a US company's open-weight models under a partnership with it](2026-08-01-innovation-meets-impact-as-minister-buthelezi-launches-batho-pele-ai-chatbot), and [voter registration ran inside the same company's messaging platform](2026-08-07-south-africa-whatsapp-voter-registration).
developments:
Two state functions moved onto one foreign platform company inside three days of each other. The public service department's [chatbot is a partnership with that company and a local supplier, built on its open-weight model family](2026-08-01-innovation-meets-impact-as-minister-buthelezi-launches-batho-pele-ai-chatbot), serving policy, circular and legislation lookups to citizens and public servants. The electoral commission [ran voter registration inside its messaging platform](2026-08-07-south-africa-whatsapp-voter-registration) for the three days before the deadline, carrying one-time-password authentication, identity-document upload and address verification, and 1.7m registration transactions over the final weekend.

Neither is a signed public commitment of the kind this indicator usually records, and that is the point: no memorandum, contract value, data-handling statement or exit arrangement is published for either. What the base holds is two live dependencies and no instrument behind them.

Separately, the enterprise AI adoption reported under sectoral systems runs on a foreign cloud provider, and the satellite entrants reported under connectivity are the same country's.

summary: A domestic bank [went live on China's cross-border payment system](2025-11-20-cips-goes-live-standard-bank-sarb-inauguration) and was [jointly authorised as renminbi clearing bank for Africa](2026-06-26-standard-bank-icbc-renminbi-clearing-bank-africa); a [disability-data plan was agreed](2026-08-12-south-africa-china-disability-inclusion-data-cooperation).
developments:
2025-11-20 — a domestic bank [went live as the first African direct participant in China's cross-border interbank payment system, inaugurated at the central bank](2025-11-20-cips-goes-live-standard-bank-sarb-inauguration) with both countries' central bank governors present.

2026-06-26 — the same bank and a Chinese state bank were [jointly authorised as renminbi clearing bank for Africa](2026-06-26-standard-bank-icbc-renminbi-clearing-bank-africa), covering the nineteen African countries where the group operates. The designation was made by one foreign central bank with no African regulator party to it.

2026-08-12 — outside payments, a [seven-point plan on disability-inclusive data, universal design and assistive technology was agreed](2026-08-12-south-africa-china-disability-inclusion-data-cooperation), naming the national statistics office as a partner with no instrument or data-sharing arrangement published.

The engagement is deepest where it is least visible as policy: the payments arrangements are commercial acts by a listed bank, authorised abroad, and no domestic instrument records or governs them.

summary: Team Europe [announced a package of nearly EUR 12 billion covering digital connectivity among other areas](2025-10-09-team-europe-south-africa-investment-package), and [the science and technology committee met for the eighteenth time](2026-06-18-18th-eu-south-africa-jstcc-meeting).
developments:
2025-10-09 — [a package of nearly EUR 12 billion was announced covering digital connectivity among other areas, building on EUR 4.7 billion announced at the March summit](2025-10-09-team-europe-south-africa-investment-package), at which [the two sides committed to cooperate on artificial-intelligence governance and the Global Digital Compact](2025-03-13-8th-south-africa-eu-summit-declaration).

The digital share of the package is not itemised anywhere on the record, so what reaches connectivity is not derivable from it — which is the standing difficulty with headline figures of this kind.

2026-06-18 — [the joint science and technology cooperation committee met for the eighteenth time, marking thirty years of the bilateral agreement, with commitments on wider research-programme participation and bilateral artificial-intelligence cooperation](2026-06-18-18th-eu-south-africa-jstcc-meeting).

summary: Satellite connectivity services [entered operation through a domestic venture and a United Arab Emirates operator](2026-06-30-brainsat-and-thuraya-services-launch), framed against the national broadband programme.
developments:
2026-06-30 — [satellite connectivity services entered operation in Johannesburg through a domestic venture and a United Arab Emirates operator, using that operator's next-generation and broadband infrastructure, framed against the national broadband programme and rural connectivity](2026-06-30-brainsat-and-thuraya-services-launch). No capacity, price, coverage or subscriber figure is published, and no licence instrument is named.

The formal machinery of the relationship is old: [the second session communique of the bilateral joint commission is the base's only record of it](2018-10-22-sa-uae-joint-commission-2nd-session-communique), eight years before this launch, with no later session or digital workstream on file.

So the engagement that delivered a service has no visible instrument behind it, and the instrument on record has delivered nothing this base can name.

summary: Indian industry [committed to expanding investment including in technology during the deputy president's visit](2026-06-02-mashatile-secures-investment-commitments-during-india-visit), and [a province studied India's procurement marketplace](2026-04-15-kzn-treasury-engages-india-on-digital-procurement-reform).
developments:
2026-06-02 — [Indian industry committed to expanding investment in South Africa including in information and communications technology during the deputy president's visit, with engagements involving the Indian technology industry association and a trade and technology council](2026-06-02-mashatile-secures-investment-commitments-during-india-visit). These are commitments by industry rather than by government, with no value or instrument published, against [a 2016 joint statement as the standing bilateral frame](2016-07-08-sa-india-joint-statement-modi-visit).

2026-04-15 — [a provincial treasury engaged the Government of India on its government electronic marketplace, drawing on Indian digital public-procurement experience to inform provincial reform](2026-04-15-kzn-treasury-engages-india-on-digital-procurement-reform). It is knowledge exchange rather than a binding instrument, and it is the only case on this ledger of a province conducting its own digital diplomacy.
